doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Chicago and New York with Dizzy Gillespie
title: Carnegie Hall and Boston with Chano Pozo
summary: He recalls suggesting Chano Pozo's jungle outfit and chant, the next night at Boston's Symphony Hall, and the difficulty communicating with Chano.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And then he does the next 16 bars after the introduction, right?
Yeah.
Okay. And I was wondering, was that what you were talking about?
Yeah, and then after that, it was all mine, after he – Chano – I suggested to Dizzy in a bus going up from New York to Boston that he should have Chano come out and his “yanyow” thing.
[Daughtry sings.] Yeah, his chant.
[Russell sings.] He did that. But Dizzy hadn’t thought of doing that. I told him, have him put on his jungle outfit. He came out in this theater downtown here, this music hall . . .
In Boston here?
The Strand?
The music hall here in Boston.
Oh, Massey. Not Massey?
Yeah.
Not here. No, that’s in Toronto. Umm . . .
Oh, that’s right.
Only thing I can think of is a club.
The Strand Theater.
Where the Boston Symphony Orchestra plays. You know. That’s easily – that’s easy to see.
Alzheimer’s.
These things – we haven’t thought about these things, and they are way at the back of the mind. If we sit here now for ten minutes, we’ll get it.
It will come to us at some point.
I can – it’s not Carnegie Hall. Carnegie Hall was the big performance, the first performance of the piece. The next night . . .
Symphony Hall is where?
Oh, it’s something like . . .
Something like that. All I can think of is that club that they’re always talking about. But you’re talking about a hall, right?
No, it’s called Symphony something.
Symphony Hall. That’s all.
Is that it?
I think it’s Symphony Hall in Boston. Symphony Hall, yeah. So, the night after he opened at Carnegie Hall as the first jazz . . .
Modal composition.

. . . artist to do that, to play at that place, we went in a bus to Boston, and Symphony Hall was the next. Chano came out in his jungle stuff. Brothers were all sitting in the front. They started laughing.
How did you all communicate with Chano? Because he couldn’t speak any English, from what I understand.
We didn’t communicate. You had to prepare yourself for a serious conversation, okay? A very serious conversation, especially if it involved money.
So I get the sense it was confrontational.
Yes, confrontational is a good way to put it.
